'''Victor Galitski''' is an American [[physicist]], a [[theorist]] working in the area of [[quantum physics]].

==Education and career==
Galitski  earned his PhD in applied math (under Prof. Dmitry Sokoloff <!-- <ref>http://www-old.srcc.msu.ru/nivc/english/about/inf/sokoloff.html {{Bare URL inline|date=May 2022}}</ref>--> from the Math Faculty in [[Moscow State University]]) and a {{not a typo|2<sup>nd</sup>}} PhD in quantum physics under Prof. [[Anatoly Larkin]]. Galitski was later a postdoctoral fellow  at the [[Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics]]. <!-- working with [[Matthew P. A. Fisher]].--> He has been on the faculty at the [[University of Maryland]] since 2005, where he is now a Chesapeake Chair Professor of Theoretical Physics. He is also a Fellow of the [[Joint Quantum Institute]] there, an [[Honorary title (academic)|honorary professor]] at [[Monash University]] in [[Melbourne]], [[Australia]], and a foreign partner of the Australian [[ARC Centre of Excellence in Future Low-Energy Electronics Technologies]] (FLEET). <!-- <ref>https://www.monash.edu/science/schools/physics/about/ourpeople {{Dead link|date=February 2022}}</ref>-->  <!-- <ref>http://www.fleet.org.au/team/ {{Bare URL inline|date=May 2022}}</ref><ref>https://umdphysics.umd.edu/about-us/news/department-news/1205-cnam-and-jqi-members-on-team-awarded-33m-from-australian-research-centre.html {{Bare URL inline|date=May 2022}}</ref>-->

Galitski has been awarded the [[National Science Foundation CAREER Awards|NSF career award]], [[Simons Foundation|Simons Investigator award]],<ref>Peter Coclains, "Immigrant Scientists Enrich the U.S.," Wall Street Journal, July 28, 2013 [https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424127887323309404578613703855242698] 
</ref> the [[Open Society Foundations|Open Society Fellowship]], and the [[Australian Research Council|Future Fellowship from Australian Research Council]].
His notable researches include the 2010 prediction of [[topological insulator|topological Kondo insulators]].<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.104.106408| pmid = 20366446| title = Topological Kondo Insulators| journal = Phys. Rev. Lett.| volume = 104| issue = 10| article-number = 106408| year = 2010| last1 = Dzero | first1 = M. |display-authors=etal| arxiv = 0912.3750| bibcode = 2010PhRvL.104j6408D| s2cid = 119270507}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1038/492165a| pmid = 23235853| title = Hopes surface for exotic insulator| journal = Nature| volume = 492| issue = 7428| page = 165| year = 2012| last1 = Reich | first1 = Eugenie Samuel| bibcode = 2012Natur.492..165S| doi-access = free}}</ref><ref>Natalie Wolchover, "Paradoxical Crystal Baffles Physicists," Quanta Magazine [https://www.quantamagazine.org/samarium-hexaboride-crystal-blurs-metal-insulator-line-20150702/]</ref> In 2006, he introduced  a new kind of spin-orbit coupled [[Bose-Einstein Condensate]].<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevA.78.023616| title = Spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensates| journal = Phys. Rev. A| volume = 78| issue = 2| article-number = 023616| year = 2008| last1 = Stanescu | first1 = T. D. |display-authors=etal| bibcode = 2008PhRvA..78b3616S| arxiv = 0712.2256| s2cid = 10273804}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1038/nature11841| pmid = 23389539| title = Spin–orbit coupling in quantum gases| journal = Nature| volume = 494| issue = 7435| pages = 49–54| year = 2013| last1 = Galitski | first1 = V.| last2 = Spielman | first2 = I.| arxiv = 1312.3292| bibcode = 2013Natur.494...49G| s2cid = 240743}}</ref> 
In 2007, together with University of Maryland coworkers including [[Sankar Das Sarma]], Galitski resolved the  minimal conductivity puzzle in [[graphene]] physics.<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1073/pnas.0704772104| pmid = 18003926| pmc = 2141788| title = A self-consistent theory for graphene transport| journal = PNAS| volume = 104| issue = 47| pages = 18392–18397| year = 2007| last1 = Adam | first1 = S. |display-authors=etal| bibcode = 2007PNAS..10418392A| arxiv = 0705.1540| doi-access = free}}</ref> Together with Gil Refael, Galitski co-introduced [[Floquet theory|Floquet]] [[topological insulators]].<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1038/nphys1926| title = Floquet topological insulator in semiconductor quantum wells| journal = Nature Physics| volume = 7| issue = 6| pages = 490–495| year = 2011| last1 = Lindner | first1 = N. |display-authors=etal| arxiv = 1008.1792| bibcode = 2011NatPh...7..490L| s2cid = 26754031}}</ref><ref>David L. Chandler, MIT News Office (October 24, 2013) "Persuading light to mix it up with matter," https://news.mit.edu/2013/persuading-light-to-mix-it-up-with-matter-1024</ref> <!-- Recently, he has developed new interests in modeling [[hydrodynamics]] and [[turbulence]] in electronic materials.<ref>Victor Galitski, Mehdi Kargarian, and Sergey Syzranov, Phys. Rev. Lett. '''121''', 176603 (2018), "Dynamo Effect and Turbulence in Hydrodynamic Weyl Metals" [https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.121.176603] </ref><ref> Anna Demming, "Benchtop cosmology exploits solid-state systems," https://phys.org/news/2018-10-fast-flowing-electrons-mimic-astrophysical-dynamos.html</ref> --> 

In July  2021, Galitski published a viral essay on linkedin, entitled "Quantum Computing Hype is Bad for Science,"<ref>V. Galitski, "Quantum Computing Hype is Bad for Science," https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/quantum-computing-hype-bad-science-victor-galitski-1c/?trackingId=WOuRqwByRr6JL00V9sXWDQ%3D%3D</ref> cautioning about  unsupported, inflated claims in the quantum computing industry and the dangerous possibility of "quantum Ponzi schemes."

==Family background==
Victor Galitski was born in [[Moscow]], [[Russia]] in a family of  Jewish, German, and Russian  ancestry. His grandfather Victor Galitskii ({{ill|Галицкий,_Виктор_Михайлович|ru}}) was a renowned  physicist,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ghassib |first1=H. B. |last2=Bishop |first2=R. F. |last3=Strayer |first3=M. R. |date=1976-05-01 |title=A study of the Galitskii-Feynman T matrix for liquid 3He |journal=Journal of Low Temperature Physics |language=en |volume=23 |issue=3 |pages=393–410 |doi=10.1007/BF00116928 |s2cid=121402516 |issn=1573-7357}}</ref><ref>"Total energy from the Galitskii-Migdal formula using realistic spectral functions," https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.62.4858</ref><!--<ref> Online Encyclopedia (in Russian) [https://web.archive.org/web/20150521100842/http://mosenc.ru/encyclopedia?task=core.view&id=11038]</ref>--> who worked with [[Lev Landau]],<ref>V.M.Galitskii, [[Lev Landau|L. D.Landau]], and [[Arkady Migdal|A.B.Migdal]], "The disintegration of the deuteron by the Coulomb field of the nucleus," Physica '''22''', 1168 (1956)
 [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0031891456901628?via%3Dihub]</ref> and [[Arkady Migdal]], and was director of the theoretical physics department in the [[Kurchatov Institute]].
